outcome: congenital anomalies of the kidneys and urinary tract (CAKUT)
cohort: The study included 411,055 babies (from 204,167 mothers) born between 1980 and 2009 in Saskatchewan, comprising both First Nations and non-First Nations individuals.
finding: Pregestational diabetes (pre-G/DM) was an independent predictor of CAKUT, particularly in non-First Nations individuals and in First Nations individuals with maternal history of stillbirth, and CAKUT was strongly associated with a more than 100-fold increased likelihood of ESRD, accounting for 40% of ESRD cases in young people.
followup_time: Up to 34 years (births from 1980 followed until 2014)
